record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.original_question: Do recent strangeness measurements in high-energy nuclear collisions, especially strange-antibaryon enhancement at CERN-SPS, indicate new physics associated with local color deconfinement, or can the data be explained by known phenomena without invoking quark-gluon plasma formation?

evidence.quote: Do any of the recent strangeness results suggest the presence of new physics, or can we deal with these data on the basis of known phenomena, without invoking the local color deconfinement? A clear answer to this question is, in my opinion not available yet, but a number of highly noteworthy experimental and theoretical results are pointing in the direction of QGP, we have here discussed in depth the enhancement of antibaryons which has been observed at CERN-SPS in the way it has been predicted.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions (such as Pb–Pb collisions at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron), one observes an enhanced production of strange antibaryons (anti-Λ, anti-Ξ, anti-Ω) relative to a baseline of proton–proton or proton–nucleus collisions scaled by the number of participating nucleons. A long-standing theoretical prediction asserts that such an enhancement, increasing with the strangeness content of the (anti)baryon, is a signature of a transient deconfined phase of matter (the quark–gluon plasma, QGP) in which colored quark and gluon degrees of freedom are locally liberated and chemically equilibrate strangeness on short timescales via gluon fusion.

Problem. Determine whether the observed pattern of strangeness production in high-energy nucleus–nucleus collisions, and in particular the hierarchical enhancement of multi-strange antibaryons, requires the formation of a locally color-deconfined phase (quark–gluon plasma) for its explanation, or whether it can be accounted for quantitatively by purely hadronic mechanisms (e.g., hadronic rescattering, canonical strangeness suppression in small systems, string-fusion or color-rope models, and baryon–antibaryon annihilation effects) without invoking deconfinement. Provide either (i) a hadronic-phase dynamical model that reproduces, within experimental uncertainties, the magnitudes, strangeness-hierarchy, system-size, energy, and centrality dependence of the measured strange and multi-strange (anti)baryon yields; or (ii) an argument showing that no such hadronic explanation is possible and that QGP formation is necessary.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent experimental and theoretical work, culminating in the CERN 2000 announcement and RHIC/LHC results, established a broad consensus that strange-antibaryon enhancement together with other observables is consistent with QGP formation in heavy-ion collisions; multi-strange hyperon enhancement is now widely considered an established QGP signature. However, alternative or complementary hadronic explanations (e.g., canonical suppression, baryon–antibaryon annihilation effects, and recent observations of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions by ALICE) continue to be actively investigated, so the specific question of whether QGP is strictly required is not fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Strangeness and quark–gluon plasma — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The CERN WA97 experiment demonstrated enhancement of particles with one, two and three strange (anti)quarks, in time for the CERN 2000 announcement of possible QGP formation.
status_evidence.claim: Strange-antibaryon enhancement at CERN-SPS was a key QGP signature confirmed by WA97 and contributed to the 2000 announcement of a new state of matter.

status_evidence.title: Impact of baryon anti-baryon annihilation on strangeness enhancement at SPS energy
status_evidence.snippet: Recent study (2025) re-examines hadronic baryon–antibaryon annihilation contributions to strangeness enhancement at SPS.
status_evidence.claim: Hadronic mechanisms competing with QGP-based explanations of strange-antibaryon enhancement remain under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: QGP Signatures revisited, Eur. Phys. J. C (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: A 2024 review revisits the QGP signatures including strangeness enhancement.
status_evidence.claim: The interpretation of strangeness signatures of QGP is still being refined in recent literature.
